open.title: THE BLUEPRINT + LIVE RE-SOLVE ARCHITECTURE — WILL, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenar
open.full: the blueprint + live re-solve architecture — will, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenario that people try and memorize, i want that for us, so we can try searching for the most similar scenario from a repository as well as live rollout"*, alongside *"i dont want to behavior clone first i want to try our searching and poker like simulation"*. this is the architecture that beat humans at nlhe — libratus and pluribus do not play off charts, they compute a coarse blueprint offline and do real-time subgame re-solving at the table. blueprint + live search is exactly what he described, and it is a far better fit here than behaviour cloning: vgc-bench trains offline so inference is cheap, whereas search pays per turn on a clock. the endgame half is already scoped and small — #47 measures 1v1 at 16 cells, 2v1 at 96, 2v2 at ~1,296, with 2v1 alone reachable in 45.9% of games; retrograde analysis builds up from there (#30, #40, #41). the early game is the research problem and it is the abstraction, not the retrieval. poker charts work on isomorphism — a(s)k(s) and a(h)k(h) are one hand — and pokemon has no isomorphism that clean, because which species is on the field is the information content. so the repository needs a learned similarity metric. we have a candidate and it has been tested in the wrong direction: #23 gated porygon2 on whether it can separate positions two turns apart; retrieval needs the inverse, that genuinely similar positions land close. same encoder, opposite test, never run. the honest dependency: the re-solve half needs a fast simulator, which loops back to #62 and to the poke-env benchmark nobody has ever taken

open.title: THE END GOAL, STATED SO PRIORITIES CAN BE ARGUED AGAINST IT — WILL, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sh
open.full: the end goal, stated so priorities can be argued against it — will, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sheets and get to number 1 on the ladder but we are far off"*. it had never been written down, so every ordering argument in this register was being made against a target nobody had stated. it is a curriculum, not a mismatch — will corrected this the same day: *"once we solve open team sheets, we can think about the more difficult closed team sheets and adapt our models accordingly"*. i first filed the open-sheet corpus against a closed-sheet target as a violation of this file's *fitting environment must match playing environment* rule. that was an over-application. the rule governs fitting and playing in the same deployment; deliberately solving the fully-observable version first and adapting afterwards is staging, and staging is how you get a measurable baseline at all. what survives is narrower and still worth holding: a model fitted where every set is known must be able to accept uncertainty about sets later, and that is an architecture question better answered before everything is built assuming certainty — the same lesson as the focus sash drag, where replacing a hedge with a certainty inherited responsibility for every event that staled it. and it flips the poker argument the right way. open sheets strip out most hidden information and make our game easier than poker in the dimension poker is hardest; closed sheets put it back — unknown items, spreads, the fourth move, which four of six they brought — so information sets become the game and #163's blueprint+re-solve becomes the right primitive rather than a flourish. two things already built for other reasons are the closed-sheet machinery: #52 hypno (rate the opponent, decide how hard to exploit — deferred by will) and the prefer observed over declared rule with its knock off / trick / consumed-berry tracking, which is exactly the inference a closed-sheet bot needs. will's own farigiraf/cud chew read is the same idea from the player side: a bluff that exists only because sheets are closed, and that open sheets delete. "far off" is accurate — #62 unanswered, ~26 open rows in the medicham block, no search redesign started

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: ARGMAX IS UNSOUND IN A SIMULTANEOUS-MOVE GAME, AND OPEN TEAM SHEETS DO NOT RESCUE IT — CITED, 2026-08-11. Bosansky, Lisy
open.full: argmax is unsound in a simultaneous-move game, and open team sheets do not rescue it — cited, 2026-08-11. bosansky, lisy, lanctot, cermak & winands, *algorithms for computing strategies in two-player simultaneous move games*, artificial intelligence 237 (2016) 1-40: agents *"may need to use randomized (or mixed) strategies in order to play optimally ... even though the only information that is hidden is each player's action as they play it"*. simultaneity alone forces mixing. i had told will the opposite — that open sheets make our game easier than poker in poker's hardest dimension. on this axis they do not. what medicham is: `miltank.js:1315` is `if (v > bestval) { bestval = v; bestpair = [ia, ib]; }` and `:1384` clicks it — a plain argmax, deterministic by construction, answerable for free by anyone who knows the scorer. magnemite underneath it does sample (`magnemite.js:954`, `:1154`, a softmax its own header calls *"the single biggest measured lever"* and which argues *"taking the argmax would be the obvious thing and it is wrong here"*), so the bot gets less mixed as it gets smarter — the 31.6% of turns miltank defers are the only ones that come out mixed, which inverts #62: more compute means fewer deferrals means more predictable. duct is not the fix — i had it in the fix list and the paper reports it *"also might not converge to a nash equilibrium"*, even the mixed variant; uct's failure is shown on biased rock-paper-scissors (shafiei, sturtevant & schaeffer, giga 2009). what is sound, three tiers from that paper: exact backward induction solving the matrix game per node, which *"outputs a subgame perfect ne"*; sm-oos, which *"guarantee[s] to closely approximate the optimal strategies given enough time"*; and sm-mcts-rm (regret matching at simultaneous nodes) as the practical middle. so roadmap #41's python equilibrium solver is the textbook-correct primitive for this game class, currently filed as *"the equilibrium answer exists and cannot play"*. and unlike pluribus we are 1v1 zero-sum, so the *"equilibrium is not the right goal"* retreat does not apply to us — equilibrium is the target here. phase 3, not now: medicham is phase 1 and a correct simulator is a prerequisite under every version of this. registered so it is not rediscovered

only meowscarada learns it), plus compound eyes, no guard and tangled feet as accuracy rows. none of these is unstageable. every one is in the wrong instrument | closed 2026-08-11 — the staged arm shipped and the proc sampler is right. `engine/million_run.js --staged` -> `data/million-run-staged.json`, release `eafb0abb9736`, free-running dice. 17 fixtures covering all 12 proc target rows plus 5 the target list does not carry. pooled over every row that fires: 58,738 of 176,209 against 58,613.76 expected, z = +0.64, every row powered to one point. denominator known by construction and proved so by a trigger-control arm that must record zero trials — `millionrun_sabotage=staged-precondition` shows it red (13 of 17 controls went 0 -> 60 trials, refused). will's stopping rule, and it answers the question nobody could: 241,525 staged battles / 63 seconds for 1-point resolution; 78,494 / 21 s for 2 points; 19,758 / 6 s for 5. a staged battle is one constructed four-body board played for one turn at 0.26 ms — not comparable to a self-play game, which is why 'a million games' was always the wrong unit. the rule earned itself immediately: at 2 points effect spore read 31.90% and diverged at 95%, with a split-half spread of 1.97 against an effect of 1.90 — not an effect (lessons §9) — and at the powered n it reads 30.34%. a row stopped early is not a smaller answer, it is a different one. and the instrument's own three bugs were found before publication: the first version matched the tag's status word against the engine's and read flame body 0/40 and poison point 0/40 — a headline that would have been filed against engine — because the tag speaks `burn`/`poison`/`sleep` and the engine speaks `brn`/`psn`/`slp`, and static passed by pure accident on three shared letters; open.full: mag becomes a futility gate and stops being a learned scorer — will, 2026-08-13. *"im thinking of cutting mag back in size to say, no fake out after turn 1, no poison on steel, no status moves into gholdengo, no prio moves when farig is on the board... just very simple rules and not the whole convoluted, protect and let my partner ko the threat."* this fixes an ordering fault and is not merely a simplification. a learned mag prunes what is bad on average and runs before doduo, so it deletes precisely the actions that are bad alone and good in combination — fake out into a spread, follow me covering a setup turn, a weak click that baits a protect — which is the entire class doduo exists to find. the safe line is futile (no other action rescues it) versus bad (conditional, must survive to doduo). the gate must be derived, not written, and all four example rules are wrong as typed: fake out is `activemoveactions > 1` — first turn out, not turn 1 of the game, so a fake out user switching in on turn 6 may still use it; corrosion (salazzle, glimmora) poisons steel; good as gold is `breakable` and refuses only when `target !== source`; armor tail is one of farigiraf's three abilities and exempts perish song, flower shield and rototiller. category right every time, hand-written form wrong every time — the ban-list-of-four shape, and a prune list is worse than a ban list because it fails silently: a deleted option leaves no trace in any output. so the gate asks the engine "does this action produce any effect on this board" rather than holding rules. open sheets do not remove the need: fake out's condition is battle state and appears on no sheet, and the sheet stops being true — six legal moves change an ability mid-battle plus 11 mold breaker carriers and a mummy, and knock off has 4,078 corpus uses. it reads the live board, which on turn one is the same object and by turn four is not. buildable now — the only stage of the pipeline with no fitted parameters, so the quarantine does not block it. needs a counter for what it pruned and a check that a pruned action really was a no-op: an over-pruning gate deletes a good play and nothing catches it, because both sides of every comparison share the blind spot

open.full: the word "endgame" is claimed by two models in our own ledger, and that is why the architecture was hard to hold — will, 2026-08-13. *"wait didnt we have dusknoir as the endgame guy? its hard to keep track."* he is right and the confusion is ours, not his memory. `docs/models.md:1451` scopes dusk as the endgame tablebase — exact, precomputed offline, shipped as a lookup because it cannot be solved under a turn timer. slowking's job: line in the same file reads *"the endgame — tell you the equilibrium-best move (and win %) on a live position"*, which is not distinguishable in wording. the split, now written down: dusk is small endgames, exact, offline then looked up; slowking is any position, approximate (an equilibrium over estimated values), live per turn; hypno is about the opponent rather than the position and is a deliberate deviation from slowking. only dusk can say "guaranteed" — which means will's own description of the late-game stage (*"which ones lead to a guaranteed win... hand these scenarios to miltank"*) is dusk's job and was filed under hypno. fixed in `docs/models.md` and `docs/alakazam-v2-spec.md`. and the matrix is kept even if greedy wins: *"id still want slowking matrix even if greedy wins right? because then if we play opponents regularly we can adapt and become unexploitable."* keeping it is right and is already adr-003's position — vgc-bench's policy beats a worlds competitor and is ~100% exploitable, so winning on average and being safe are different axes. one correction to the reasoning: adapting to an opponent makes you more exploitable, not less. nash never adapts and cannot be beaten in the long run; deviating to punish a habit opens a hole in you. what repeated play actually buys is the other direction — a fixed policy degrades because they learn you, and greedy is a fixed mapping. the matrix is not the adaptation mechanism; it is the floor you measure your deviations against, and hypno is the deviation

open.title: EVERY HAZARD LANDS ON THE SIDE THAT LAID IT IN THE OFFLINE BOARD, AND THE LIVE PATH IS RIGHT — SO THE FIT AND THE GAME D
open.full: every hazard lands on the side that laid it in the offline board, and the live path is right — so the fit and the game disagree. found by search 2026-08-13 while chasing #249; split out and verified independently. `engine/board.js` `notemove` ends with `if (move.sidecondition) board.startside(side, move.sidecondition, ...)` — `side` is the mover's, unconditionally. derived from the format, not recalled: of the 11 legal side-condition moves in this regulation, seven are `target: allyside` and four are `target: foeside` — stealth rock, spikes, sticky web, toxic spikes. the seven (reflect, light screen, aurora veil, safeguard, tailwind, quick guard, wide guard) are correct by accident, because the mover's side is the right answer for them. the four hazards are recorded on the layer's own side, which is the side they can never be on. this is not #249 and must not be closed with it. that row is the seed carrying no hazards into a playout — a missing feature, and a rollout that ignores hazards is merely blind. this is a feature that is present and inverted, and it sits in the board the fit reads: `engine/board.js` is the offline board, the live path reads showdown's `|-sidestart|` and gets it right. that is fitting environment and playing environment must match, broken in a new place — the same shape as mag fitted with the sheet visible and played without it, and machamp trained under broken mega. a model fitted on a board where stealth rock hurts its own team learned something about a game nobody plays. size, and it is small and that is not the argument: 259 corpus uses across the four (stealth rock 168, sticky web 42, toxic spikes 34, spikes 15) against 16,074 for tailwind alone. a wrong value is worse than a missing one at equal volume, because nothing downstream can tell it is wrong. the fix is derived, not a list of four: read `move.target` and place the condition on the far side when it is `foeside`. a hand-written hazard list here would be the ban-list-of-four shape a third time, and a hazard added next regulation would silently land on the wrong side again. three sites, not one, and they are currently wrong together — which is the only reason nothing has broken. read 2026-08-13 before anyone touches it: `engine/board.js:2675` writes with `board.startside(side, ...)`; `:3311` reads with `board.hasside(side, m.sidecondition)` to set `deadside` ("this move cannot work, it is already up"); `:3343` reads the same way for `alreadyup`, which gates `setupturns`. all three take the mover's side, so today they are self-consistent and the error cancels — a hazard is written to the wrong side and then looked for on that same wrong side. fixing the write alone produces a worse bug than the one it fixes: the hazard would land on the foe's side while both readers keep looking at the mover's, so `deadside` would never fire for a hazard and the model would re-lay stealth rock every turn believing it was not up, crediting itself `setupturns` each time. so it is one helper, not three edits — a single `sidefor(board, side, move)` that answers "whose side does this condition live on" from `move.target`, called by the write and by both reads. whose side a condition lands on is a fact, and three call sites must not each decide it independently; that is the rule this repo has broken most expensively. `const foeside = side === 'p1' ? 'p2' : 'p1'` is already an idiom at five other places in the same file, so the helper has a shape to match. a probe must cover both directions: a hazard laid by p1 is readable by p1 as "up on the far side" and must still set `deadside` when p1 tries to lay it again. a probe that only checks placement passes on an engine that placed it right and can no longer see it. closed 2026-08-13 by measure, and the row understated the blast radius by six sites. `sidefor(side, move)` lives in `engine/board.js` beside the class, is exported, and is called by nine sites: the write at `notemove`, the two reads (`deadside`, `alreadyup`), and six verbatim copies of the same mover's-side derivation found by engine's sweep — `engine/fit_policy.js:793` (the fit itself), `joint_rows.js`, `branch_recall.js`, `corpus_shift.js`, `feature_coverage.js`, `redirect_audit.js`. fixing only the three in `board.js` would have left the fit reading a board where a hazard hurts the team that laid it, which is the whole defect wearing a different file name. one correction to this row, measured rather than repeated: "crediting itself `setupturns` each time" is wrong. none of the four hazards carries a `condition.duration` (reflect 5, tailwind 4, the hazards none), so `dur()` returns 0 and `setupturns` is 0 for them under every variant. the observable movement is `deadside` alone; the `alreadyup` site is routed through the helper for the one-fact-one-function rule and binds today only on the seven `allyside` moves, where `sidefor` is the identity. the finding that outlives the fix is the guard's. `tests/test-feature-semantics.js` was structurally blind to this: run under both boards with the old fixture, 0 of 76 hashed columns moved, because `engine/feature_fixture.js` contained zero hazard clicks and pre-set only `reflect` and `tailwind` — both `allyside`, exactly the half the fix leaves alone. a new board, `hazards-already-up`, puts `stealthrock`/`spikes` up on p2 and `stickyweb`/`toxicspikes` up on p1 so the flip is exercised in both directions, and `deadside` now moves `b984c210828d -> d1be4f95d589` with nothing else moving. red proofs, all three by compiling a pre-#254 `board.js` in memory and injecting it — the tree was never reverted: `tests/test-hazard-side.js` 5 passed / 3 failed at head and 11/0 after; the semantics guard's new clause names all six wrong candidates; and reverting one of the six sweep sites fails the ninth-site clause by file name. `tests/test-mechanics.js` 565 live / 0 missing, unmoved, as expected — the whole-game differential exercises `medicham2`, not the feature board. and the refit verdict is no, measured: the fit is bit-identical and this was only ever a live-play defect. the whole fit corpus was replayed through `fp.decisionsfor` under both boards — 9,226 games, 237,052 decisions, 1,731,851 candidate vectors, 0 errored, identical decision key set — and 0 decisions, 0 games and 0 feature vectors move. the reason is not thin exposure alone (24 hazard clicks: sr 19, toxic spikes 2, sticky web 2, spikes 1; 258 decisions carry a hazard candidate) but an isomorphism, constructed rather than argued: `notemove` wrote to the mover's side and both readers read the mover's side, so the old board is the new one with the two sides relabelled, and every offline-derived read agrees. the mismatch is against a state that did not come from `notemove` — which is the live path. `engine/magnemite.js:647` takes the side straight off `|-sidestart|` and calls `notemove(..., worked=false)`, so on the pre-#254 board a hazard laid by p1 read `deadside` p1=0, p2=1 — the layer re-lays stealth rock forever believing it is not up, and the victim refuses to lay its own believing it is. fixed: p1=1, p2=0. same probe, offline arm: identical under both boards for all 11 moves. so mag was fitted where `deadside` was effectively right and played where it was backwards — fitting-and-playing-environment-must-match broken in a new place, and closed in the one direction that costs no refit

open.title: GOOD AS GOLD REFUSES ALLY-AIMED STATUS MOVES IN THE AUTHORITY AND OURS ONLY REFUSES FOES — 2026-08-13, LEFT BY THE #241
open.full: good as gold refuses ally-aimed status moves in the authority and ours only refuses foes — 2026-08-13, left by the #241 pass rather than half-fixed. the handler's condition is `move.category === "status" && target !== source`, so it refuses anything that is not the holder itself — including a partner's decorate, coaching, skill swap or heal pulse, measured on the authority. every branch here is `_isfoe`-gated, so a gholdengo accepts support from its own side that showdown refuses. this is a refusal defect, not an emission one, which is exactly why it was correct to leave it: #241 parts (1) and (2) were a narration pass, and folding a behaviour change into them would have made a three-game differential move unattributable. and it is a real set, not a curiosity — gholdengo is the single carrier and ally-aimed support into your own gholdengo is ordinary doubles play. fix it with its own before/after. closed 2026-08-13, and the sweep doubled the scope the row stated. derived first: one carrier in the regulation (gholdengo, filtered walk) and `refusesstatusmoves` has exactly one member over the whole tag corpus (`abilities:goodasgold`, 3,043 uses), printed before anything was wired. the authority was measured one battle per route — a supporter aiming at its own partner — and 26 routes all print `|-immune|p1b: gholdengo|[from] ability: good as gold`, including the untargetable ones (life dew, howl, heal bell, perish song, teeter dance, corrosive gas); not refused in the same sweep: tailwind, light screen, safeguard, trick room, misty terrain, haze, because a side and a field are not a body. against that, 35 ally routes were played on this engine: 19 were already right and nine were wrong in two shapes — five branches gated the call on `_isfoe` (`boostally`, `reorder`, `abilityswap`, `abilitywrite`, `statrewire`; a partner's skill swap walked away with good as gold) and four had no refusal at all (`helpinghand`, life dew's arm of `heal`, howl's arm of `boostally`, and `perish`). `perish` was therefore wrong for a foe gholdengo too — no `_isfoe` audit could have found it, because there was no gate to audit. fixed by making the one announcer side-blind (`tryhitrefusal` already carried `t!==m`, which is `target !== source`) and calling it per body in the spread branches, so howl still lifts the user and perish song still marks the other three; `pranksterblocked` keeps its own foe gate inside that function because the authority gates it there, so this widens one ability and nothing else. new counter `medseen.tryhitrefusedally`. the probe was wrong before the engine was, twice: it read the `|move|` line as an effect (it names the target in field 4), and — the one that mattered — its exemption arm was a self-aimed nasty plot, which routes to `kind:'setup'`, a branch that never asks about a refusal, so deleting the `t===m` exemption outright left the probe green. every self route now goes through a branch this change edited. red proof in both directions: exemption deleted -> `564/1` naming all four self routes; `_isfoe` restored on `boostally` alone -> `564/1` naming `decorate`, with the pre-existing foe-side decorate probe still live. census 564 -> 565 live / 0 missing. whole-game differential, 1,220-game pinned pair, both arms, releases `0c5bb83c5744` -> `9b25e830df49` verified to differ in one file: top 254 -> 253, bottom 294 -> 293, `unrelated event mismatch` 30/26 -> 29/25 with every other class identical to the instance, and one cause gone by name — `|-immune|p2a|[from]goodasgold <> |-singleturn|p2a|helpinghand`, a real game where the authority refused a helping hand at a gholdengo and we applied the mark. no new causes; normalised lines compared rose 1,507,925 -> 1,509,557, which is what removing an early stop looks like. one game per arm is the instrument's reach, not the fix's size — the swarm aims 828 of ~46,700 clicks at an ally across 1,220 games and only the fraction landing on the one carrier can exercise this. `test-engine-diff.js --n 6000`: 6000 agreed, 0 disagreed, both corners

open.full: four more ontryhit refusal sites answer wrongly, named rather than swept — 2026-08-13. residue of #241, each written down instead of being folded into a pass that had already moved: role play and spite reach `kind:'pass'`, which carries no target to announce a refusal against, so the refusal has nowhere to go; heal pulse emits a second `|-fail|<mover>` on the ordinary full-hp path, so it is wrong even when nothing refused it; soundproof and overcoat announce a bare `|-immune|` where the authority names the ability. the last one is the same shape as magma armor under #239 — an ability that refuses through a route the attribution reader does not cover — so the fix is to widen `immuneattrin()`'s reach rather than to add two names. how these were found is the part to keep: a sweep over all 78 legal foe-aimed status moves x 8 bodies, 624 cases, which is what turned "the refusal is already correct and only the line is wrong" into twelve action kinds routing such a move and four distinct wrong answers, with lock-on and heal pulse carrying no refusal at all — a lock-on at a gholdengo applied its guarantee and a heal pulse healed it. the row's own sizing was right and its scope was not; the sweep is the reason that was discovered before shipping rather than after. closed 2026-08-15, all four sites, each staged against the authority and printed side by side before a line was edited. (a) role play and spite had two nowheres, not one: the terminal `{kind:'pass',mv:id}` dropped the target it was handed, so `tr.mv(m,_mid,_tt||m)` named the user in field 4 *and* there was no body for a refusal to answer against — ours `|move|p1a: meowstic|roleplay|p1a: meowstic` and nothing after it, against `|move|p1a: meowstic|role play|p2a: gholdengo` + `|-immune|p2a: gholdengo|[from] ability: good as gold`. the target is kept only for the classes the authority lets a player name a body for, read out of `sim/battle-actions.ts:3`'s own `choosable_targets` into a new `targetclass.chooseable` (360 of 500 legal moves; the read throws rather than defaulting to an empty set), and the refusal goes through the one `tryhitrefusal` announcer #241/#255 built. the other three `pass` moves are measured residue, not an oversight: fairy lock (`all`) names the user in field 4, teatime (`all`) and heal bell (`allyteam`) name it blank with `[still]`, and teatime is refused by good as gold while fairy lock is not — a different shape, written down rather than half-fixed. (b) heal pulse printed the handler's own `|-fail|<target>|heal` and then `mvfail`'s `|-fail|<mover>` under it; `healpulse.onhit` returns `this.not_fail`, so the generic fail never runs, and staged at full hp recover, rest, life dew and synthesis each print exactly one line too. fixed with `mvfailannouncedbycaller`, a separate writer rather than a flag so a call site cannot silently lose the `|-fail|` it owes; `_mvres` is deliberately unchanged because `movethisturnresult` is cleared at the turn boundary and could not be staged off a finished battle. (c) soundproof and overcoat — the row asked for `immuneattrin()` to be widened rather than for two names, and that is what landed: `immunetomoveclass.announceswith`, read off `ontryhit`/`onallytryhitside` by the same reader #239 built for `onsetstatus`. membership printed before it was wired — five carriers, four announcing (overcoat, soundproof, bulletproof, wind rider) and one not (magic bounce, which reflects) — and wind rider has no legal carrier in this regulation, which is why its conditional `-immune` (it announces only when the +1 attack fails) is a warning in the code and not a branch. the engine reads it through one function, `moveclassimmuneattr`, and the powder family gets its own `powderimmuneattr` because powder has three refusers and only one is an ability: a grass body is refused by the type chart above `ontryhit` and the authority announces it bare, which is the control arm and is what stops this being a paste. measured: forretress/sleep powder, bastiodon/snarl, chesnaught/shadow ball all name their ability; chesnaught/sleep powder stays bare. census 579 → 584 live / 0 missing across this row plus #241 and #259; three probes (`healdescriptor`, `refusesstatusmoves`, `immunetomoveclass`), each shown red first in `tests/probe_red_demo.js`, one of them against a stripped artifact field rather than a reverted line because that is where its fix lives. `tests/test-engine-diff.js --n 6000`: 6000 agreed, 0 disagreed

open.full: seventy-five silent catch blocks above the floor, 41 of them manufacturing a value, all in engine's and search's files — shrunk to its remainder 2026-08-15; measure's own files are clear. numbers re-measured on the day, not carried: run the gate for the per-file list, never this sentence. the original row, kept whole: seventy-eight new silent catch blocks since the 2026-08-06 baseline, and the gate has been red all week while every report called it pre-existing — 2026-08-13. `tests/test-no-silent-failure.js` exits 1: 744 catch blocks, 296 silent (40%), 220 baselined, 2 fixed, 78 new — and 101 of the silent ones manufacture a value, handing a made-up result downstream rather than merely skipping. that last class is this project's named failure mode in its purest form: *a capability was absent and everything reported success.* this row exists because "pre-existing" was doing the work that "known failure" used to do. three separate agent reports named this gate red and moved on, each correctly observing they had not caused it; the sum of those correct observations is a check nobody acts on, which claude.md already says is not a check. the instrument was audited first and is sound. the baseline is keyed by a hash of the catch body, not by line number, so it survives edits elsewhere and this is real debt rather than drift. reading three flagged blocks found two false positives — `engine/game_differential.js:2656` counts through `state_fails.x = (state_fails.x || 0) + 1` and `:1783` sets a null the very next line reports — so the detector gained the `(x || 0) + 1` counter idiom, the fourth such correction in that file and the same argument each time: a ratchet that flags code for doing what it asked is how a ratchet gets ignored. and the sample was misleading, which is the part to keep: two of three suggested the gate was badly over-firing; the debt is still open. both earlier figures were stale and neither was right today: 787 catch blocks, 296 silent (38%), of which 97 manufacture a value and 199 only skip or continue; 216 baselined, 80 new. of the 80 new, 41 manufacture and 39 only skip — that split is now printed, grouped by file and manufacturing-first, instead of being a flat wall of 25 names with "... and 57 more". the instrument's real defect was that it had one control and it was all-or-nothing. `--update` wrote the current silent set as the floor, so there was no way to lock in a fix without laundering every new offender in the same command — which is precisely why the row says not re-baselined, and precisely why the gate could sit red for a week while three correct reports called it pre-existing. `--update` is now monotone: it writes `min(baseline, current)` per key, so it removes what was fixed and structurally cannot add what is new. the only door into the floor is `--accept <file> "reason"`, one file at a time, with the reason recorded in the artifact beside the keys — refused outright if either argument is missing. demonstrated: `--update` lowered the floor 220 → 216 across two passes and the gate stayed red at 80 new, where the old behaviour would have written 303 and reported zero. fixed, all in measure-owned files and all of the manufacture class: `engine/provenance.js` ×3 (`declaredwriter`, `keysof`, `mtime` each turned "corrupt / permission-denied / mid-write" into the same answer as "absent" inside the tool whose job is to say whether an artifact can be believed — they now call `logunreadable`, and the count is printed every run including at zero), `engine/quarantine.js` ×2 (an unreadable artifact reported as `no artifact` to the gate that decides whether medicham is correct; (1) the differential's team pool, already filed as #81 wire 5 and stated in `engine/game_differential.js:4037` in its own words: *"`buildswarm` reads data/games.bo3.jsonl and data/games.ots.jsonl live, dedupes to distinct teams and picks by a stride over the matching set — so one appended game shifts the stride and changes which teams get played"*, with the note that both files moved during that wire's own test runs. the mitigation there asserts which team keys were picked, so a moved pool is visible afterwards; it does not stop the pool moving. `data/team-pool-frozen` already exists and is half the mechanism. open.full: five tag signatures are carried by moves the engine treats differently — so something other than the tag is deciding, and 105,709 uses sit on those signatures. generalised from #126 rather than left as one anecdote: every move in `data/tags.json` was resolved through `playeraction` on the frozen release and grouped by its sorted tag list. five groups split on the resolved kind, and a split can only mean a name match (forbidden here) or a tag missing the param that should separate them (#71). ranked: 96,406 `protect`+`detect` -> `protect` but `endure` -> `affect`, the highest-usage signature in the format carrying three behaviours — and `protectmoves` is an exported name list, which is the mechanism; 4,924 `wideguard` -> a branch, `quickguard` -> nothing (#126); 3,721 `roost`/`recover`/`slackoff`/`softboiled` -> `heal` while `wish` and `rest` -> nothing, because the tag says *heals self* and cannot express delayed or also-sleeps; 524 `beatup`/`hex`/`storedpower` -> `attack`, `spitup` -> nothing; 134 `bellydrum`/`tidyup` -> `statcode`, `acupressure` -> nothing. the last three overlap #125's dead list and groups a/b of the 13-row diagnosis, so the fix is shared. the check itself is the deliverable — it is cheap, it is derived, and it should be a gate: a signature whose members resolve to different kinds is either a name match or an under-specified tag, and both are defects by this repo's own rules

open.title: 'GOOD ENOUGH' IS A USAGE-WEIGHTED THRESHOLD, NOT A ROW COUNT — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. Will
open.full: 'good enough' is a usage-weighted threshold, not a row count — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. will, 2026-08-10: *'we do have to ask ourelves at what point is the engine good enough and has enough used features that it can perform its end goal'*. measured against the corpus rather than argued: 553,910 total move clicks; 781 (0.14%) land on a move that resolves to a whole no-op turn; 3,888 (0.70%) land on a move the roster says disagrees with the authority; the union is 4,208 = 0.76%. so 99.24% of real clicks land on a move with no known defect, and the game differential is 150/150 clean on real replayed games. the gate is a coverage standard and has been read as a sufficiency standard. its 45 open move rows are deliberately-staged edge cases, which is precisely why they survived — they barely occur. the honest test of sufficiency is roadmap #68: scale the differential from 150 games to 1,000+ real stored games. if it stays clean there, the remaining rows are polish and can run beside search work rather than blocking it, and the #99 quarantine can lift on a measured condition instead of a feeling. note the standing counter-evidence, which cuts the same way: `docs/measure.md` §0 carries a tight null at n=8,883 on the hypothesis that correctness fixes move the leaf at all

open.title: THE OPTIMIZATION PASS — hand MEDICHAM to Fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch
open.full: the optimization pass — hand medicham to fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch cannot fake. will, 2026-08-10: *'once we think medicham is good enough i plan to run some optimization programs to speed it up'* / *'handing it over to feeble 5 and saying make this go faster'*. dispatchable directly — the model is selectable per agent. the hazard is that 'faster' and 'different' are indistinguishable to a benchmark. an optimizer that shaves 30% by skipping a branch produces a beautiful number and a broken engine, and every existing test can still pass because those tests cover mechanics the branch never touches. so the pass runs three instruments, not one: `tests/bench-medicham.js` for the score (built 2026-08-10, pinned fixture, best-of-5, refuses to record a baseline under load — first reading 0.4341 ms/turn); the 500-move x 4-turn whole-board digest sweep for the verdict (2,000 cells; wire 147 used it to show only 11 moved, and that is the shape every optimization must reproduce at zero); and `tests/test-damage-stages.js` at 1728/1728 exact so arithmetic shortcuts cannot drift. sequencing, which decides how much work this is: the classifier cascade is both the most likely optimization target and the thing the remaining ~20 wires append to. restructure it first and the queued fixes land in the restructured version; do the wires first and the optimizer rewrites code that was just written

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE COST OF A FEATURE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHICH PATH IT SITS IN, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10.
open.full: the cost of a feature depends entirely on which path it sits in, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10. will: *'how many of these features will slow down the engine? cause if it costs nothing to have harvest in there, then sure we can, but if there is a time cost to it then maybe we otta reconsider'* — the right question, and the answer splits cleanly. hot path — runs on every click of every rollout: the damage chain and the ~40-branch classifier cascade. tonight's five wires cost +6.2% (0.776 -> 0.825 ms/turn, interleaved a/b across frozen releases under load), and the per-hit damage loop is almost certainly all of it, being the only wire that touched damage. cold path — fires once per turn on a trigger, and is effectively free: harvest, cud chew, cheek pouch, quick guard, the heal family. so harvest specifically: yes, free. the thing to actually guard is compounding — 6% per five wires, twenty more wires, and the engine is ~25% slower to serve 0.76% of clicks. that trade stops being worth it well before the queue empties, which is the argument for #76's ratchet firing on every wire rather than at the end

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: A FEW MILLION SELF-PLAY GAMES TO PROVE THE SAMPLER FIRES AT THE RATE WE DECLARED — Will's idea, and the right tool for t
open.full: a few million self-play games to prove the sampler fires at the rate we declared — will's idea, and the right tool for the question it actually answers. *'once we feel our engine is good we can have it play a few million games and then determine if our rate for accuracy and secondary effects is right'*, then, on the distinction: *'correct run the million games after we determine'*. so: #132 first (is the declared number right — free, exact), then this (does the code fire at it — statistical). this catches the failure a probe structurally cannot: a probe forces the outcome to test the mechanic, so a secondary declared at 30% that a bug makes fire at 0% or 100% passes every probe and every roster row. that is claude.md's founding failure — a capability absent while everything reports success — in the one place the existing instruments are blind. cost is not a constraint: at the measured 0.4341 ms/turn and a mean 3.6-turn rollout, a million games is roughly half an hour. compare observed firing rates against the declared chances with a confidence interval per move, and expect the answer to be boring — the value is the one that is not

open.title: THE STORE REACHES FOUR FACTS AND THROWS THEM AWAY — and #68 needs every one of them. Will, reading the replay design: *'
open.full: the store reaches four facts and throws them away — and #68 needs every one of them. will, reading the replay design: *'i think multi hit moves say how many times they hit in the chat'*, *'life orb in the chat too'*, *'same with focus sash'*. all correct. `engine/durable-ingest.js` parses 30 protocol lines and drops these four: `|-hitcount|` (never read — so the differential skips 630 multi-hit rows as incomparable when the real hit count was on the wire); `|cant|` (never read — a flinched, paralysed, asleep, frozen or recharging body is simply an absent `m` event, indistinguishable from each other, 0 games in 52,089 carry a flinch marker); the `[from]` clause on chip damage — the parser tests for it to decide the damage is residual and then discards the text, so burn, sandstorm, life orb and rocky helmet all land as a bare `{t:'hp'}` with no source, and its own comment names them; `|-enditem|`, read only to infer what item a body held, never emitted as a turn event, so 'the focus sash triggered this turn' is gone. the store's event vocabulary is `b f fs hp m mega s w x`. this contradicts the project's founding principle — *store raw, analyze on top, every fact we might ever want* — at the parser. four regex arms; the raw replays can be re-pulled so no history is lost. ops work, touches no engine, and it makes #68 able to attribute a divergence instead of reporting an unexplained hp drop

open.full: position against three comparables, because the field is not empty and none of them is playing our game. vgc-bench (aamas 2026) — whose archive we already consume, and dropped from the fit for staleness (four days, mid-june, seven weeks old); `engine/corpus_shift.js` exists to measure the metagame distance and has never written an artifact. future sight ai — closed-source showdown bot, reportedly top 5% of the most popular format, matches revealed attributes to the most common set, ships a win-probability browser extension; also settles a naming question, since "future sight" is taken and this project names everything after pokémon. the pokeagent challenge (arxiv 2603.15563, neurips 2025, 100+ teams, two tracks) — by far the strongest reference of the three and not yet read. add sarantinos (arxiv 2212.13338, cambridge) as the closest published method: gen 7 random battles singles, peaked 33rd in the world, regret-minimisation opponent prediction, fills unknown properties from usage statistics, and explicitly rejects monte carlo sampling as too sample-inefficient — which is what miltank's leaf does. it also names our #29 independently: its first "biggest challenge" is keeping the team balanced, with a worked example that is the sack, and it asserts *"an ai agent cannot achieve this just by looking ahead with minmax or monte carlo tree search."* finally, its elo caveat is load-bearing for will's stated goal: comparing human and ai ratings is invalid unless they played each other — laddering with alakazam is exactly that, so the plan is sound and should say why
